def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    cities = d["cities"]
    net = d["net"]
    cost = d["cost"]
    capacity = d["capacity"]

    # set of valid directed arcs (i, j) with i != j
    arcs = [(i, j) for i in cities for j in cities if i != j]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.CITIES = pyo.Set(initialize=cities)
    model.ARCS = pyo.Set(initialize=arcs, dimen=2)

    # x[i,j] : amount transported from i to j, non-negative, bounded by capacity
    def x_bounds(m, i, j):
        return (0, capacity[(i, j)])

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.ARCS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=x_bounds)

    # Objective: minimize total transportation cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(cost[(i, j)] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in m.ARCS)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Constraint (1): flow balance per city
    #   sum_j x[k,j] - sum_i x[i,k] = demand[k] - supply[k]
    #   net[k] = demand[k] - supply[k]
    def balance_rule(m, k):
        outflow = sum(m.x[k, j] for j in cities if (k, j) in arcs)
        inflow = sum(m.x[i, k] for i in cities if (i, k) in arcs)
        return outflow - inflow == net[k]

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.CITIES, rule=balance_rule)

    # Constraint (2): capacity limits (enforced via variable bounds above,
    # but also stated explicitly as constraints for clarity)
    def cap_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.x[i, j] <= capacity[(i, j)]

    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.ARCS, rule=cap_rule)

    return model

    arcs = list(d["cost_cap"].keys())

        model.arcs,
        domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
        bounds=lambda m, i, j: (0, d["cost_cap"][(i, j)][1]),
        initialize=0.0,
    )

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(d["cost_cap"][(i, j)][0] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in m.arcs)
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    def cap_rule(m, i, j):
        return m.x[i, j] <= d["cost_cap"][(i, j)][1]
    model.capacity = pyo.Constraint(model.arcs, rule=cap_rule)

    out_terms = {p: [] for p in range(n)}
    in_terms = {p: [] for p in range(n)}
    for (i, j) in arcs:

        in_terms[j].append((i, j))

        return out_flow - in_flow == net_demand[p]
    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.city, rule=balance_rule)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    N = d["num_cities"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # City set
    model.I = pyo.RangeSet(0, N - 1)

    # Arc set: ordered pairs i != j (use list of tuples)
    arcs = [(i, j) for i in range(N) for j in range(N) if i != j]
    model.A = pyo.Set(initialize=arcs, dimen=2)

    cost = d["cost"]
    cap = d["cap"]

    def cap_rule(m, i, j):
        return (0, cap[i][j])

    # x[i,j] = amount shipped i -> j, nonnegative, bounded by route capacity
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.A, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals,
                      bounds=cap_rule)

    # Objective: minimize total transportation cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(cost[i][j] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in m.A)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Helper: net supply sign per city (positive supply, negative demand)
    supply = d["supply"]
    demand = d["demand"]

    def net_supply(i):
        return supply.get(i, 0)

    def net_demand(i):
        return demand.get(i, 0)

    # Flow balance: supply + inflow = demand + outflow
    # -> sum_j x[i,j] - sum_j x[j,i] = supply[i] - demand[i]
    def bal_rule(m, i):
        outflow = sum(m.x[i, j] for j in range(N) if (i, j) in m.A)
        inflow = sum(m.x[j, i] for j in range(N) if (j, i) in m.A)
        return outflow - inflow == net_supply(i) - net_demand(i)

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=bal_rule)

    return model

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    cities = d["cities"]
    net = d["net"]
    cost = d["cost"]
    cap = d["cap"]

    # ordered pairs (i, j) with i != j
    arcs = [(i, j) for i in cities for j in cities if i != j]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=cities, ordered=True)
    model.A = pyo.Set(initialize=arcs, dimen=2, ordered=True)

    def cap_bound(m, i, j):
        return (0, cap[i][j])

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.A, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals, bounds=cap_bound)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return sum(cost[i][j] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in m.A)

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Flow balance: sum_j x[k,j] - sum_i x[i,k] = net[k]
    def balance_rule(m, k):
        outflow = sum(m.x[k, j] for j in cities if j != k)
        inflow = sum(m.x[i, k] for i in cities if i != k)
        return outflow - inflow == net[k]

    model.balance = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=balance_rule)

    return model
